title: T1583.003 — Acquire Infrastructure - Virtual Private Server
subtitle: Watch a rented server go from crypto-paid account to blocked-and-reported C2 host in eight steps.
aria: Animated diagram: an attacker opens a VPS account with a crypto payment, deploys and hardens a Ubuntu virtual machine, installs C2 tooling, scans the target, sends a phishing lure whose implant beacons to the VPS, issues commands through the VPS, and the SOC detects the beacon by VPS ASN, blocks the IP, hunts for other beacons, and files an abuse report with the provider.

nodes.label: Attacker
nodes.tip: Pays for and controls the rented server; reaches your estate only through the VPS.

nodes.label: Provider
nodes.tip: The commercial provider. It holds the identity trail: payment method, signup IP, console logs, and the abuse team.

nodes.label: VPS
nodes.tip: The rented virtual machine on a hosting ASN. Cheap, disposable, replaced within minutes when blocked.

nodes.label: Victim
nodes.tip: The target: a workstation that beacons out and a perimeter that gets scanned.

nodes.label: SOC
nodes.tip: Security operations center connecting periodicity, hosting ASN, and reputation data.

steps.title: Crypto account
steps.caption: The attacker opens an account at a VPS provider and pays with cryptocurrency, so the account has almost no real identity behind it.
steps.defender: Nothing is visible inside your estate yet. The payment and signup happen entirely on the provider side.

detection.detail: This activity is not visible to the victim yet.

steps.title: Deploy + harden
steps.caption: The attacker deploys an Ubuntu virtual machine from a template and hardens it with key-only SSH and a default-deny firewall.
steps.defender: Still invisible. A fresh cloud VM looks identical to a developer’s test box; there is nothing to alert on yet.

steps.title: Install tooling
steps.caption: The attacker installs C2 and redirector tooling and points a young domain at the new IP with a fresh TLS certificate.
steps.defender: External sources may already see it: certificate-transparency logs and urlscan.io often record the new cert and domain before you ever see traffic.

steps.caption: The VPS scans the target edge, sending probes across many ports on the victim’s public IP ranges.
steps.defender: Firewall logs fill with denies from one hosting-ASN source. Sigma 3 counts them and asks GreyNoise whether the scan is targeted.

steps.title: Lure + beacon
steps.caption: The attacker sends a lure, the victim clicks, and the implant beacons out to the VPS on a steady 60-second schedule.
steps.defender: First real egress signal: a workstation talks to a first-seen VPS IP. Join proxy and EDR data to find the process behind it.

steps.title: Commands flow
steps.caption: The attacker issues commands through the VPS; tasking flows down and results flow back through the rented box.
steps.defender: Now a two-way channel: regular connections with small uploads. Periodicity analysis (Sigma 1 and 6) confirms the rhythm.

steps.title: SOC sees beacon
steps.caption: The SOC sees beaconing to an IP whose ASN sits on the VPS intel list and raises a beacon-plus-ASN alert.
steps.defender: Triage: confirm the enrichment, measure the rhythm, identify the owning process, and check reputation feeds before declaring an incident.

steps.title: Block, hunt, report
steps.caption: The SOC blocks the VPS IP, hunts the estate for other beacons, and files an abuse report with the provider.
steps.defender: Blocking is local and temporary; the abuse report gets the machine removed. Expect a replacement box on a new IP and hunt for it.
